title: Sorting out problems
goal: Complain about a wrong order or a faulty product, get a refund, deal with a helpline, report a stolen phone, stay calm when you're being ripped off — and tell people exactly what was said.
intro:
Things go wrong: the food delivery is wrong, the new phone dies after a day, the helpline promises a refund that never comes, someone snatches your mobile on Tariq Road. Sorting it out in Sindhi means two skills.

First, **calm, firm language**: آرام سان ڳالهايو 'let's talk calmly', توهان وعدو ڪيو هو 'you promised', مون کي پئسا واپس گهرجن 'I want my money back'.

Second, **reported speech** in full. Half of every complaint is *he said…, they told me to…, she asked whether…*. Sindhi makes this easy — after **ته** you mostly just repeat what was said — but there are a few traps: 'told me **to** wait' needs the subjunctive, and you ask **کان** someone, not کي.

grammar.title: Reporting what someone said: چيو ته …, ٻڌايو ته …
grammar.body:
To pass on what someone said, put **ته** after the speech verb and then give their words. Sindhi does **not** shift tenses the way English does:

هن چيو ته آرڊر رستي ۾ **آهي**.
He said the order **was** on its way. (lit. 'he said that the order **is** on its way')

You keep the tense the speaker used: present stays present, future stays future (هن چيو ته سڀاڻي **ايندو** 'he said he **would** come tomorrow').

**Pronouns**: very often people repeat the words exactly as spoken, even with **مان** 'I': رائيڊر چيو ته **مان** پنجن منٽن ۾ پهچان ٿو 'the rider said he'd be there in five minutes' (lit. 'said that I arrive…'). Shifting to هو (he) is also fine. Context makes it clear.

**Who was told** takes **کي**: هن **مون کي** چيو ته … 'he told me that …'; هن **مون کي** ٻڌايو ته … 'he informed me that …'.

**The verb**: چيو, ٻڌايو, پڇيو are transitive past, so the speaker is in the ergative form (مون، هن، هنن، دڪاندار، پوليس…) and the verb stays **masculine singular** — the whole ته-clause is its object. You'll also hear the suffix forms: **چيائين** 'he/she said', **چيائون** 'they said', **چيم** 'I said'.

**Hearsay**: چون ٿا ته … 'they say that…', مون ٻڌو آهي ته … 'I've heard that…'.

grammar.title: Reporting requests and orders: 'he told me to…'
grammar.body:
English says 'he told me **to wait**'. Sindhi says 'he told me **that I wait**' — **ته + subjunctive** (the present without ٿو), in the person of whoever has to do it:

هن مون کي چيو ته (مان) انتظار **ڪريان** — he told me to wait
مون هن کي چيو ته (هو) پئسا واپس **ڪري** — I told him to give the money back
هنن اسان کي چيو ته سڀاڻي **اچون** — they told us to come tomorrow
هن مون کي چيو ته فون نه **ڪريان** — he told me not to call

Don't use the future here: هن مون کي چيو ته انتظار **ڪندس** means 'he told me that **I'll** wait' (he was the one waiting!).

Two other common ways:
• **Quote the order directly** with an imperative: مئنيجر چيو ته **ڪاوڙجو نه** 'the manager said, don't get angry'.
• **Infinitive (oblique) + لاءِ چوڻ** 'to ask (someone) to': هنن مون کي فارم **ڀرڻ لاءِ** چيو 'they asked me to fill in a form'.

**Promises** work like statements: هن **وعدو ڪيو** ته سڀاڻي پئسا ڏيندو 'he promised to pay tomorrow'.

grammar.title: Reporting questions: پڇيو ته … and '… يا نه' (whether)
grammar.body:
A reported question also uses **ته** and keeps the **question word** where it was:

هن مون کان پڇيو ته آرڊر **ڪڏهن** ڪيو هو — he asked me when I had ordered
مون پڇيو ته پئسا **ڪيئن** واپس ملندا — I asked how I'd get the money back

For yes/no questions ('whether'), add **يا نه** 'or not' at the end, or start the clause with **ڇا**:
هنن پڇيو ته رسيد آهي **يا نه** — they asked whether I had the receipt
هن پڇيو ته **ڇا** وارنٽي ڪارڊ آهي — he asked if there was a warranty card

**The big trap**: you ask **کان** someone (from them), not کي:
مون دڪاندار **کان** پڇيو — I asked the shopkeeper (not دڪاندار کي)
But you **tell** کي someone: مون دڪاندار **کي** چيو / ٻڌايو.

culture:
In Sindh, problems are usually solved **person to person**, not by policy. Ask for the owner (سيٺ or مالڪ) rather than the boy at the counter, address him as **ادا** or **سائين**, and keep your voice low — shouting makes people lose face and dig in. Phrases like **آرام سان** 'calmly', **ڳالهه ٻڌو** 'listen', and **توهان پاڻ ڏسو** 'see for yourself' are your best tools. A cup of tea is often offered mid-dispute; accept it — it means the negotiation is going well.

Many shops say **'no return, no exchange'** on a sign, but a defect reported the next day with the رسيد is usually exchanged. For delivery apps and banks, the helpline is the way; keep a screenshot as **ثبوت**.

If your phone is snatched in Karachi, don't chase the snatchers. Call your network to **block the SIM**, then file a report — at the police station or through the Sindh Police online and the **Citizens-Police Liaison Committee (CPLC)**, which also helps trace phones by their IMEI number. You'll need the report for a duplicate SIM.

lessons.title: What the helpline told me

tip.title: He said that… — چيو ته
tip.body:
- Speech verb + **ته** + the words, **no tense change**: هن چيو ته آرڊر رستي ۾ **آهي** = he said it **was** on its way.
- People often keep **مان** from the original words.
- چيو / ٻڌايو stay masculine singular; the listener takes **کي**: هن **مون کي** ٻڌايو ته …
tip.pattern: هن (مون کي) چيو / ٻڌايو ته + their words

lessons.title: They told me to…

tip.title: Told me to… = ته + subjunctive
tip.body:
- 'He told me **to wait**' = هن مون کي چيو ته انتظار **ڪريان** (that I wait).
- Use the person who has to act: مون هن کي چيو ته واپس **ڪري**.
- Not the future: ته انتظار ڪندس would mean someone else waits.
- Or: فارم **ڀرڻ لاءِ** چيو = asked me to fill in a form.

sentences.en: They asked me to show proof.

sentences.native: مون هن کي سمجهايو ته اهو منهنجو آرڊر ناهي.
sentences.roman: moṃ hun khe samjhāyo ta uho munhinjo ārḍaru nāhe.
sentences.en: I explained to him that it wasn't my order.

sentences.native: ثبوت لاءِ رسيد موڪليو.
sentences.roman: sabūta lāi rasīda moklyo.
sentences.en: Send the receipt as proof.

sentences.native: هن مون کي چيو ته پريشان نه ٿيان.
sentences.roman: hun moṃ khe chayo ta pareshānu na thiyāṃ.
sentences.en: He told me not to worry.

sentences.native: مهرباني ڪري هڪ ڀيرو ٻيهر چيڪ ڪريو.
sentences.roman: meharbānī kare hika bhero ɓiyahar cheku karyo.
sentences.en: Please check once more.

lessons.title: Faulty goods and refunds

tip.title: He asked whether… — پڇيو ته … يا نه
tip.body:
- Reported questions keep the question word: پڇيو ته **ڪڏهن** آيو.
- 'Whether' = **… يا نه** at the end.
- You ask **کان** someone: مون دڪاندار **کان** پڇيو — not کي.

new: هنن پڇيو ته رسيد آهي يا نه.

sentences.native: مون دڪاندار کان پڇيو ته وارنٽي آهي يا نه.
sentences.roman: moṃ dukāndāra khāṃ puchhyo ta vāranṭī āhe yā na.
sentences.en: I asked the shopkeeper whether there was a warranty.

sentences.native: هن مون کان پڇيو ته فون ڪڏهن ورتو هو.
sentences.roman: hun moṃ khāṃ puchhyo ta fon kaɗahiṃ varto ho.
sentences.en: He asked me when I had bought the phone.

sentences.native: مون پڇيو ته هي فون اصلي آهي يا نقلي.
sentences.roman: moṃ puchhyo ta hī fon aslī āhe yā naqlī.
sentences.en: I asked whether this phone was genuine or fake.

sentences.native: امان پڇيو ته ڪيترا پئسا واپس مليا.
sentences.roman: amāṃ puchhyo ta ketirā paisā vāpasi milyā.
sentences.en: Mum asked how much money I got back.

sentences.native: هنن پڇيو ته نقص ڇا آهي.
sentences.roman: hunan puchhyo ta naqsu chhā āhe.
sentences.en: They asked what the fault was.

sentences.native: هن فون ۾ نقص آهي.
sentences.roman: hin fona meṃ naqsu āhe.
sentences.en: This phone has a defect.

sentences.native: وارنٽي ختم ٿي وئي آهي.
sentences.roman: vāranṭī xatmu thī vaī āhe.
sentences.en: The warranty has run out.

sentences.native: ڪاوڙ ڪرڻ جو ڪو فائدو ناهي.
sentences.roman: kāvaṛi karaṇa jo ko fāido nāhe.
sentences.en: There's no point getting angry.

sentences.native: نقلي سامان وٺڻ جو ڪهڙو فائدو؟
sentences.roman: naqlī sāmānu vaṭhaṇa jo kahiṛo fāido?
sentences.en: What's the point of buying fake stuff?

lessons.title: A stolen phone
new: ٻه ڇوڪرا منهنجو موبائيل کسي ويا!
مون کي ايف آءِ آر داخل ڪرائڻي آهي.
مهرباني ڪري منهنجي سم بلاڪ ڪري ڇڏيو.

sentences.native: سگنل تي منهنجو موبائيل کسي ويا.
sentences.roman: signala te munhinjo mobāilu khasī vayā.
sentences.en: They snatched my phone at the traffic light.

sentences.native: پوليس مون کان پڇيو ته چور ڪيئن هئا.
sentences.roman: pulīsa moṃ khāṃ puchhyo ta chora kīeṃ huā.
sentences.en: The police asked me what the thieves looked like.

sentences.native: ٿاڻي وارن چيو ته ايف آءِ آر جي ڪاپي سنڀالي رکو.
sentences.roman: thāṇe vāran chayo ta ef āī ār jī kāpī sambhālī rakho.
sentences.en: The police station said to keep the copy of the FIR safe.

sentences.native: مون پهريان سم بلاڪ ڪرائي.
sentences.roman: moṃ pahiryāṃ sima blāk karāī.
sentences.en: First I got the SIM blocked.

sentences.native: بئنڪ کي فون ڪري ڪارڊ به بلاڪ ڪرايو.
sentences.roman: bainka khe fon kare kārḍu bi blāk karāyo.
sentences.en: Call the bank and get the card blocked too.

sentences.native: هنن مون کي چيو ته ٻه ڏينهن انتظار ڪريان.
sentences.roman: hunan moṃ khe chayo ta ɓa ɗīṃha intizāru karyāṃ.
sentences.en: They told me to wait two days.

sentences.native: ان جو ذميوار ڪير آهي؟
sentences.roman: un jo zimevāru ker āhe?
sentences.en: Who is responsible for that?

sentences.native: ڪمپني چيو ته اسين ذميوار ناهيون.
sentences.roman: kampanī chayo ta asīṃ zimevāru nāhyūṃ.
sentences.en: The company said they weren't responsible.

sentences.native: شڪر آهي، توهان کي ڪجهه نه ٿيو.
sentences.roman: shukur āhe, tavhāṃ khe kujhu na thiyo.
sentences.en: Thank God nothing happened to you.

lessons.title: Keeping calm, not getting conned
new: آرام سان ڳالهايو، مسئلو حل ٿي ويندو.

sentences.native: ڪاوڙجو نه، سائين. آرام سان ڳالهايون.
sentences.roman: kāvaṛjo na, sāīṃ. ārāma sāṃ ɠālhāyūṃ.
sentences.en: Please don't get angry, sir. Let's talk calmly.

sentences.native: هن دڪاندار مون کي ٺڳيو.
sentences.roman: hin dukāndāra moṃ khe ṭhaɠyo.
sentences.en: This shopkeeper ripped me off.

sentences.native: اهو ميسيج ڌوڪو آهي، ڪنهن کي پنهنجو پاسورڊ نه ٻڌايو.
sentences.roman: uho mesej dhoko āhe, kanhin khe panhinjo pāsvarḍ na ɓudhāyo.
sentences.en: That message is a scam — don't tell anyone your password.

sentences.native: هن چيو ته مان بئنڪ مان آهيان. ڪوڙو هو!
sentences.roman: hun chayo ta māṃ bainka māṃ āhiyāṃ. kūṛo ho!
sentences.en: He said he was from the bank. He was lying!

sentences.native: مون کي ڪاوڙ ته آئي، پر مون آرام سان ڳالهايو.
sentences.roman: moṃ khe kāvaṛi ta āī, para moṃ ārāma sāṃ ɠālhāyo.
sentences.en: I did get angry, but I spoke calmly.

sentences.native: رڪشا وارا ڪڏهن ڪڏهن ٺڳن ٿا، ڪرايو پهريان پڇو.
sentences.roman: rikshā vārā kaɗahiṃ kaɗahiṃ ṭhaɠan thā, kirāyo pahiryāṃ puchho.
sentences.en: Rickshaw drivers sometimes rip you off — ask the fare first.

sentences.native: ٺيڪ آهي، اڌ پئسا هاڻي ۽ اڌ ڪم کان پوءِ.
sentences.roman: ṭhīku āhe, adhu paisā hāṇe ai adhu kama khāṃ poi.
sentences.en: OK — half the money now and half after the job.

sentences.native: ادا، ڪوڙو وعدو نه ڪريو.
sentences.roman: adā, kūṛo vaʿdo na karyo.
sentences.en: Brother, don't make false promises.
